units.grammar: PAST TENSE REVIEW. Past simple = finished actions (single or repeated) at a known past time: We moved to Seville in 2019. Past continuous = an action in progress at a past moment, often interrupted by a past simple action: I was cooking when the lights went out.
existing_questions_sample: While I ____ (walk) home, it started to rain. | was walking
We ____ (not see) that film yet. | haven't seen
The train ____ (already / leave) when we got to the station. | had already left
When I was little, I ____ have a red bike. (used to / would) | used to
Correct it: Did you used to play chess? | Did you use to play chess?
They ____ (wait) for two hours and they are still waiting. | have been waiting
I ____ (break) my arm last summer. | broke
I can't find my keys. I think I ____ them. (lost / 've lost) | 've lost
His eyes were red because he ____ (cry) for an hour. | had been crying
Correct it: I have seen him yesterday. | I saw him yesterday.
Every Sunday Gran ____ bake us a cake. (would / was) | would
I didn't ____ (use) to like olives, but now I love them. | use

units.grammar: COMPARATIVES AND SUPERLATIVES. Short adjectives take -er / the -est; longer ones take more / the most (or less / the least): This street is quieter, but that one is more convenient. Learn the irregular forms: good - better - best, bad - worse - worst, far - further - furthest.
vocab: get on like a house on fire
have a roof over your head
existing_questions_sample: This is ____ (bad) film I've ever seen. | the worst
My sister drives ____ (carefully) than my brother. | more carefully
Tickets cost double this year: they are ____ more expensive. (slightly / far) | far
The more you practise, the ____ (good) you get. | better
Correct it: She is more tall than me. | She is taller than me.
Flats here are getting more and ____ expensive. (one word) | more
He is ____ the fastest runner in the school. (by far / much) | by far
Tom arrived ____ (early) than anyone else. | earlier
The exam wasn't ____ hard as I expected. (as / than / more) | as
That was ____ (interesting) talk of the whole week. | the most interesting
Correct it: It's the most cheapest phone. | It's the cheapest phone.
He plays the piano ____ (well) than he did last year. | better

units.grammar: MODAL VERBS: REVIEW. Deduction: must + infinitive = you are almost sure it's true; can't = almost sure it's impossible; may / might / could = it's possible: Her light is on, so she must be in. Permission: ask with can, could or may (could and may are more polite); give it with can and refuse it with can't.
existing_questions_sample: You ____ wear a helmet on a motorbike; it's the law. (must / might) | must
The museum is free, so you ____ pay. (mustn't / don't have to) | don't have to
He's only ten. He ____ be the new teacher! (can't / mustn't) | can't
You ____ touch that wire; it's dangerous. (mustn't / needn't) | mustn't
She isn't answering. She ____ be asleep, but I'm not sure. (might / must) | might
You ought ____ see a doctor about that cough. (one word) | to
____ I borrow your pen, please? (May / Must) | May
Correct it: You should to rest more. | You should rest more.
They've been travelling all day. They ____ be exhausted. (must / can't) | must
Correct it: She musts leave now. | She must leave now.
Next year we ____ (will / have) to choose our subjects. | will have
We've got plenty of time, so we ____ hurry. (needn't / mustn't) | needn't

units.grammar: MODALS IN THE PAST. Past deduction: must have + past participle (almost sure it happened), can't have (almost sure it didn't), may / might / could have (perhaps it did). For a negative possibility use may not have or might not have. Past permission: could / couldn't or was / were allowed to: We were allowed to stay up late at weekends.
vocab: weigh up the pros and cons
apply for (a job / a place at university / an apprenticeship)
be offered (a job / a place at university)
existing_questions_sample: The ground is wet. It ____ (must / rain) last night. | must have rained
There's a bus strike today, so he ____ have come by bus. (can't / must) | can't
I failed the test. I ____ (should / study) harder. | should have studied
The door was locked, but I ____ get in through a window. (could / managed to) | managed to
Yesterday we ____ (have to) wear a suit for the photo. | had to
You ____ have brought wine; we already had lots. (needn't / couldn't) | needn't
Correct it: She must has forgotten. | She must have forgotten.
When I was five, I ____ already swim. (could / managed) | could
I don't know where Leo is. He ____ have missed the train. (might / can't) | might
As children we ____ (not / allow) to watch TV late. | weren't allowed
Correct it: You shouldn't have tell him. | You shouldn't have told him.
It was a holiday, so I ____ get up early and slept till ten. (didn't have to / mustn't) | didn't have to

units.grammar: THE FUTURE. Present simple for timetables (The ferry sails at nine) and after time words such as when, as soon as, until: I'll text you when I land. Present continuous for fixed arrangements: I'm seeing the dentist on Friday. will for predictions, future facts, promises, offers, refusals and instant decisions. going to for intentions and for predictions based on something you can see now.
existing_questions_sample: The train ____ (leave) at 6.15 tomorrow morning. | leaves
I'll call you as soon as I ____ (arrive). | arrive
Look at those black clouds! It ____ rain. (is going to / will) | is going to
This time next week I ____ (lie) on a beach. | will be lying
By June we ____ (finish) all our exams. | will have finished
'The phone's ringing.' 'OK, I ____ get it.' ('ll / 'm going to) | 'll
Be quiet! The concert is about ____ (start). | to start
Correct it: When he will come, we'll eat. | When he comes, we'll eat.
We ____ (meet) Sara at eight tonight; it's all arranged. | are meeting
We ____ going to have a barbecue, but it rained. (one word) | were
By 2030 she ____ (work) here for ten years. | will have been working
Correct it: I promise I call you. | I promise I'll call you.

units.grammar: GERUNDS AND INFINITIVES. Some verbs are followed by to + infinitive: afford, agree, decide, hope, manage, offer, promise, refuse: We agreed to share the bill. Others are followed by -ing: admit, avoid, consider, deny, enjoy, finish, keep, miss, risk, suggest, can't stand, look forward to: He keeps interrupting.
existing_questions_sample: We can't afford ____ (buy) a new car. | to buy
She avoided ____ (answer) my question. | answering
I'm looking forward to ____ (see) you. | seeing
I'll never forget ____ the sea for the first time. (to see / seeing) | seeing
Remember ____ the lights off when you leave. (to turn / turning) | to turn
He's very good ____ fixing computers. (in / at / on) | at
Correct it: I suggest to take a taxi. | I suggest taking a taxi.
She left without ____ (say) goodbye. | saying
We stopped ____ (buy) some water and then drove on. | to buy
It was impossible ____ (hear) the speaker. | to hear
____ (eat) too much sugar is bad for you. | Eating
My head hurts. Have you tried ____ an aspirin? (to take / taking) | taking

units.grammar: CONDITIONALS. Zero: if + present, present = something that is always true: If you press this, it beeps. When the if clause comes first, put a comma after it. First: if + present, will / may / might = a likely future result. unless means if not: We'll be late unless we run. Second: if + past simple, would / could + infinitive = an unlikely or imaginary present or future: If I were you, I'd apologise.
existing_questions_sample: If you heat ice, it ____ (melt). | melts
If it rains tomorrow, we ____ (stay) at home. | will stay
If I ____ (have) more money, I'd travel the world. | had
If she had studied, she ____ (pass) the exam. | would have passed
You won't pass ____ you work harder. (unless / if) | unless
If I ____ (be) you, I'd say sorry. | were
Correct it: If it will rain, I'll stay. | If it rains, I'll stay.
If we ____ (leave) earlier, we wouldn't have missed the bus. | had left
If I hadn't eaten so much, I ____ (not feel) sick now. | wouldn't feel
If he ____ so lazy, he would have finished yesterday. (wasn't / isn't) | wasn't
I ____ (call) you if I had known your number. | would have called
Plants die if they ____ water. (don't get / won't get) | don't get

units.grammar: WISH AND IF ONLY. wish + past simple or past continuous = you are unhappy about a present situation: I wish I had a bigger room. wish + past perfect = regret about the past: I wish I had brought a coat. wish + could + infinitive = something you would like to be able to do but find difficult: I wish I could dance.
existing_questions_sample: I wish I ____ (know) the answer, but I don't. | knew
I wish I ____ (not eat) so much last night. | hadn't eaten
I wish you ____ stop tapping your pen! (would / did) | would
If only I ____ (can) play the guitar. | could
She wishes she ____ (have) a sister. | had
I got soaked. I wish I ____ my umbrella this morning. (took / had taken) | had taken
Correct it: I wish I can fly. | I wish I could fly.
If only it ____ stop raining! (would / will) | would
If only we ____ so far from the beach. (didn't live / don't live) | didn't live
He wishes he ____ (listen) to his mum's advice last year. | had listened
I wish my brother ____ keep taking my clothes. (wouldn't / won't) | wouldn't
Correct it: I wish I didn't go yesterday. | I wish I hadn't gone yesterday.

units.grammar: CLEFT SENTENCES. A cleft sentence splits one idea into two parts so that one piece of information stands out. What-clause + is / was + noun phrase: What I need is a holiday. You can also begin with All: All I want is some peace. What + subject + do / did + is / was + infinitive emphasises an action: What she did was call the police. After verbs like want or intend keep to: What I want is to sleep.
vocab: fulfil (an ambition, a dream, a goal, requirements)
submit (an application, an essay, homework, a proposal)
existing_questions_sample: ____ I need is a good night's sleep. (one word) | What
It was my brother ____ broke the window. (who / which) | who
It ____ in 2015 that we moved here. (was / were) | was
What I love about her ____ her sense of humour. (is / are) | is
Rewrite: I want a pizza. What I ____ a pizza. | want is
Rewrite: The noise woke me. It ____ woke me. | was the noise that
What he did ____ call the police. (was / did) | was
Correct it: What I need it is time. | What I need is time.
Correct it: It was Tom which phoned. | It was Tom who phoned.
It was in Paris ____ they first met. (that / what) | that
Rewrite: She only wants some peace. All she ____ some peace. | wants is
It's the waiting ____ I can't stand. (that / what) | that

units.grammar: INVERSION. In formal or dramatic style, a negative or limiting expression at the start of a sentence is followed by question word order (auxiliary + subject + verb): Never have I seen such a mess. Negative starters: never, not once, at no time, under no circumstances, no way, not since, not only ... but also. Limiting starters: little, rarely, seldom, hardly, only then, only when, not until.
existing_questions_sample: Never ____ I seen such a beautiful sunset. (one word) | have
Rarely ____ so much homework. (we get / do we get) | do we get
Not only ____ she sing, but she also dances. (does / is) | does
Under no circumstances ____ you open this door. (should / you should) | should
Correct it: Never I have felt worse. | Never have I felt worse.
Little ____ he know what was waiting for him. (did / was) | did
Rewrite: I had never felt so happy. Never ____ so happy. | had I felt
Only when the bell rang ____ we leave. (did / had) | did
Correct it: Not once he did say sorry. | Not once did he say sorry.
Not until I got home ____ my phone was missing. (did I realise / I realised) | did I realise
No way ____ I going to pay that much! (am / do) | am
Rewrite: We rarely eat out. Rarely ____ out. | do we eat

units.grammar: THE PASSIVE. Form: be in the right tense + past participle. Only verbs that can take an object have a passive. Use it to focus on the person or thing affected: The bridge was built in 1900. It works in all tenses and after modals: is being repaired, has been sold, had been stolen, will be sent, must be signed. In informal English get can replace be: My bike got stolen.
vocab: Your eyes are bigger than your stomach.
existing_questions_sample: Spanish ____ (speak) in many countries. | is spoken
The thief ____ (arrest) last night. | was arrested
Our classroom ____ (paint) at the moment. | is being painted
The invitations ____ (already / send), so it's too late to change them. | have already been sent
The results ____ (announce) tomorrow. | will be announced
All phones must ____ (switch) off during the exam. | be switched
The Mona Lisa was painted ____ Leonardo. (by / from) | by
Correct it: The window was broke yesterday. | The window was broken yesterday.
Rewrite: Someone has stolen my bag. My bag ____. | has been stolen
When I arrived, the room ____ (still / clean) by the staff. | was still being cleaned
Informal: My phone ____ stolen on the bus. (got / did) | got
By the time we arrived, all the food ____ (eat). | had been eaten

units.grammar: PASSIVE GERUND & INFINITIVE. Verbs that take a to-infinitive take the passive infinitive to be + past participle (She hopes to be chosen); verbs that take -ing take being + past participle (He avoids being seen). Use to be + past participle after adjectives: I was glad to be invited. Use be + past participle after modal verbs: The flight might be cancelled.
existing_questions_sample: I hate ____ (tell) what to do. | being told
She expects ____ (promote) soon. | to be promoted
The match might ____ (cancel) because of the snow. | be cancelled
He insisted on ____ (pay) in cash. | being paid
I was happy ____ (invite) to the wedding. | to be invited
____ (choose) for the team was a big surprise. | Being chosen
Nobody enjoys ____ at. (being laughed / to be laughed) | being laughed
Correct it: I want to being informed. | I want to be informed.
Rewrite: They gave Ana a medal. Ana ____ a medal. | was given
Rewrite: They sent me an email. An email was sent ____ me. (one word) | to
Correct it: She hates be criticised. | She hates being criticised.
The rules must ____ by everyone. (be followed / being followed) | be followed

units.grammar: CAUSATIVES. have + object + past participle = you arrange for somebody else to do a job: I had my bike repaired. The same pattern describes bad things that happen to you: She had her phone stolen. get + object + past participle means the same but is more informal: I must get my jacket cleaned.
existing_questions_sample: I'm going to have my hair ____ (cut) tomorrow. | cut
We got the car ____ (repair) last week. | repaired
Our teacher made us ____ (stay) after class. | stay
My parents let me ____ (go) to the concert. | go
I'll get my brother ____ (help) us move the sofa. | to help
Correct it: She made me to cry. | She made me cry.
He had his wallet ____ on the metro. (stolen / steal) | stolen
I'll have my assistant ____ (send) you the file. | send
Correct it (a painter did it): I had painted my room. | I had my room painted.
Dad won't ____ me stay out late. (let / make) | let
You should get your eyes ____ (test). | tested
The dentist ____ me open my mouth wide. (made / got) | made

units.grammar: REPORTED SPEECH. Tenses usually move one step back (am - was, have done - had done, did - had done, will - would, can - could). The past perfect, would, could and should stay the same. The word that is optional. No tense change is needed if the words are still true or if the reporting verb is in the present: She says she's tired.
existing_questions_sample: 'I'm hungry.' He said he ____ hungry. | was
'I'll help you.' She said she ____ help me. | would
'We've finished.' They said they ____ finished. | had
'I saw it yesterday.' He said he had seen it the day ____. | before
She suggested ____ a taxi. (to take / taking) | taking
He offered ____ me home. (to drive / driving) | to drive
He apologised ____ being late. (for / of / about) | for
Correct it: He said me the truth. | He told me the truth.
'I'll be here tomorrow.' He said he'd be ____ the next day. | there
The doctor advised me ____ (rest). | to rest
Tom denied ____ the window. (breaking / to break) | breaking
It ____ (say) that the castle is haunted. | is said

units.grammar: RELATIVE CLAUSES. who / that for people, which / that for things, whose for possession, where for places, when for times, why for reasons. whom is formal and used after prepositions. Defining clauses give essential information and have no commas. When the pronoun is the object of the clause you can drop it: The film (that) we saw was great.
existing_questions_sample: The woman ____ lives next door is a vet. (who / which) | who
That's the boy ____ dog bit me. (one word) | whose
This is the town ____ I was born. (one word) | where
My mum, ____ is 50, runs marathons. (who / that) | who
Can 'that' be left out? The book that I bought was cheap. (yes / no) | yes
Correct it: The man which called was rude. | The man who called was rude.
I'll never forget the day ____ we met. (when / where) | when
He failed the test, ____ surprised everyone. (which / what) | which
Formal: The person to ____ I spoke was helpful. (one word) | whom
Correct it: Madrid, that is huge, is fun. | Madrid, which is huge, is fun.
That's the reason ____ I left early. (why / which) | why
Which type of relative clause needs commas? (defining / non-defining) | non-defining

units.grammar: PARTICIPLE CLAUSES. Present participle (-ing) clauses describe an action at the same time as, or just before, the main action, or its result: Opening the door, she saw a stranger. Both parts must share the same subject. They can follow conjunctions and prepositions such as while, after, before, since, on: After leaving school, he moved abroad.
existing_questions_sample: ____ (walk) along the beach, I found a ring. | Walking
____ (finish) her homework first, she then went out. (perfect participle) | Having finished
____ (build) in 1850, the bridge is still in use. | Built
The man ____ (stand) by the door is my uncle. | standing
The phones ____ (make) in this factory are exported. | made
____ (not know) the way, we got lost. | Not knowing
____ by the noise, the baby started to cry. (Frightened / Frightening) | Frightened
She sat by the fire, ____ a book. (reading / read) | reading
Rewrite: Because I was tired, I left. ____ tired, I left. | Being
After ____ (leave) school, he moved to London. | leaving
Correct it: Having ate, we went out. | Having eaten, we went out.
____ in simple English, the book is easy to read. (Written / Writing) | Written
